subtitle: Stone Wheels, Silent Sun: Timekeeping at Konark

panels.shot: epic low-angle wide of a single Konark wheel under blazing coastal sun
panels.action: Shilpa-Surya stands in shadow beside a gigantic carved stone wheel of Konark, his palm hovering near a spoke as the noon sun burns over the Odisha coast.

dialogue.text: At Konark, c.1250 CE, architects carved 24 stone wheels for Surya—but scholars now ask: did these wheels also tell the very hour of the sun?

i18n.hi: कोणार्क में, लगभग १२५० ई., शिल्पियों ने सूर्य के लिए २४ पत्थर के पहिये गढ़े—अब विद्वान पूछते हैं: क्या ये पहिये सूरज की घड़ी भी थे?

panels.shot: bird’s-eye over temple complex and Bay of Bengal
panels.action: From high above, the incomplete yet towering stone chariot of the Sun Temple rises from the sands near the Bay of Bengal, its walls crowded with sculpture and its massive wheels aligned along the platform.

dialogue.text: On the Odisha coast, the Eastern Ganga kings raised a stone chariot for Surya. Around its base, twenty-four vast wheels wait in silence, carved with a precision that still puzzles scholars.

i18n.hi: ओडिशा तट पर, पूर्वी गंग राजाओं ने सूर्य के लिए पत्थर का रथ उठाया। उसके चारों ओर, चौबीस विशाल पहिये मौन खड़े हैं, इतनी नाप-तोल से बने कि आज भी विद्वान हैरान हैं।

panels.shot: slow push-in on one monumental wheel
panels.action: A single Konark wheel fills the frame, its rim crowded with fine reliefs, its eight main spokes and many smaller ones catching sharp sunlight and throwing a clean shadow on the platform.

dialogue.text: Debala Mitra measured them—huge circles of stone, roughly three meters across, with eight bold spokes and finer ribs. Ornament, yes. But the geometry seems deliberate.

i18n.hi: देबाला मित्रा ने उन्हें नापा—पत्थर के विराट गोले, लगभग तीन मीटर फैलाव, आठ मोटे तिल्ले और बारीक धारियाँ। सजावट तो है, पर इसकी ज्यामिति सोची-समझी लगती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shilpa-Surya examining a palm-leaf manuscript
panels.action: Inside a dim pillared hall, Shilpa-Surya sits cross-legged by a window, unrolling a palm-leaf manuscript with geometric diagrams, while a shaft of light cuts across his thoughtful face.

dialogue.text: The architects of Konark did not write their names in stone. We remember them through traces—a geometry of circles and squares, and manuscripts on architecture and astronomy preserved elsewhere.

i18n.hi: कोणार्क के शिल्पियों ने अपना नाम पत्थर पर नहीं लिखा। हम उन्हें निशानों से पहचानते हैं—गोले और चौकों की ज्यामिति से, और वास्तु व ज्योतिष के ग्रंथों से जो कहीं और बचे हैं।

panels.shot: close-up of diagrams on palm leaf: circles, rays, squares
panels.action: The palm leaf shows a carefully incised circle inscribed in a square, radiating lines like rays; beside it, neat Odia script with rules on proportion and orientation.

dialogue.text: Texts like Shilpasarini and later vastu treatises speak of circles within squares, alignments to the cardinal directions, and the journey of the sun. Konark’s plan follows this language in stone.

i18n.hi: शिल्पसारिणी जैसे ग्रंथ और बाद के वास्तु-शास्त्र में चौकों के भीतर गोले, दिशाओं की रेखाएँ और सूरज की यात्रा का वर्णन है। कोणार्क की रचना वही भाषा पत्थर में बोलती है।

panels.shot: architect’s-eye top-down drawing morphing into temple base
panels.action: A hand sketch on cloth of the temple platform and wheel positions fades into the actual carved base on site, where craftsmen chip away at sandstone blocks set along a straight axis.

dialogue.text: The temple is set on a strong east–west axis. The main shrine once opened to the rising sun over the sea. The wheels hug the sides of this cosmic chariot, their positions tied to that line.

i18n.hi: मंदिर सख्त पूर्व–पश्चिम धुरी पर रखा गया है। मुख्य गर्भगृह कभी समुद्र के ऊपर उगते सूरज की ओर खुलता था। ये पहिये इसी ब्रह्मांडीय रथ की देह से चिपके हैं, उसी रेखा से जुड़े हुए।

panels.shot: wide shot of eastern facade at sunrise
panels.action: At dawn, the sun lifts over the Bay of Bengal, casting long shadows across the eastern facade, where the front wheels glow in orange light while others remain in deeper shade.

dialogue.text: Each morning, light swept along the stone. Today, scholars like S. Balachandra Rao stand here and ask: do the wheels’ shadows mark the passing hours on this oriented wall?

i18n.hi: हर सुबह, रोशनी पत्थर पर बहती थी। आज, एस. बालचंद्र राव जैसे विद्वान यहाँ खड़े पूछते हैं: क्या पहियों की परछाइयाँ इस दीवार पर गुजरते घंटे दिखाती थीं?

panels.shot: medium shot of Shilpa-Surya testing shadow with a rod
panels.action: Shilpa-Surya kneels by a half-carved wheel, holding a straight rod along a spoke while watching how the sun’s light casts a crisp shadow across the rim.

dialogue.text: Indian astronomers had long used gnomons and shadows. At Konark, instead of a simple vertical stick, the very spokes and rims may have been shaped to catch and measure those shifting lines.

i18n.hi: भारतीय ज्योतिषियों ने लंबे समय से शंकु और छाया का इस्तेमाल किया था। कोणार्क में, साधारण डंडे की जगह शायद तिल्ले और किनारे ही उन बदलती रेखाओं को थामने और नापने के लिए गढ़े गए।

panels.shot: diagrammatic side view blending art and sun path
panels.action: An overlay shows the side wall with a wheel; below, the low winter sun and high summer sun paths, with arrows indicating changing shadow angles on the carved rims.

dialogue.text: Rao’s study plots the sun’s path, the wall’s orientation, and the wheel’s form. He argues that, together, they allow the shadow’s tip to fall near particular spokes at particular times.

i18n.hi: राव का अध्ययन सूरज की चाल, दीवार की दिशा और पहिये की बनावट को जोड़ता है। उसका कहना है कि इन्हें मिलाकर छाया की नोक खास समय पर खास तिल्लों के पास गिरती है।

panels.shot: tight close-up on rim carvings: minute divisions
panels.action: The rim of the wheel is shown in detail, dotted with small, evenly spaced motifs and larger markers at the junctions of main spokes, like a finely graded scale in stone.

dialogue.text: Eight major spokes, smaller divisions between them, and subtle markers on the rim—Mitchell and Mitra’s measurements reveal a regularity that invites reading as a dial rather than random decoration.

i18n.hi: आठ मुख्य तिल्ले, उनके बीच छोटी-छोटी बाँटें, और घेरे पर हल्के निशान—मिचेल और मित्रा की नाप से जो नियमितता दिखती है, वह इसे सजावट से ज्यादा एक घड़ी की पट्टी बना देती है।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shilpa-Surya directing sculptors
panels.action: On the scaffolding, Shilpa-Surya points to a chalk line on a wheel while sculptors work with chisels, the sea wind tugging at his garments as he aligns his arm with the sun’s direction.

dialogue.speaker: the_architects_of_konark
dialogue.text: Keep the spokes true to the east and west. Let Surya’s own rays measure them.

i18n.hi: तिल्लों को सच्चे पूर्व और पश्चिम की ओर रखो। सूरज की किरणें ही इन्हें नापें।

panels.shot: conceptual montage of 24 wheels and 24 hours
panels.action: A sequence of wheels along the temple base morphs into a band of 24 segments, each linked to a simple sun symbol, suggesting an association with the full cycle of a day.

dialogue.text: There are twenty-four wheels. Tradition speaks of Surya’s chariot, its seven horses and cosmic journey. Modern readers see another layer: twenty-four hours, plotted in sacred stone.

i18n.hi: यहाँ चौबीस पहिये हैं। परंपरा सूरज के रथ, उसके सात घोड़े और ब्रह्मांडीय यात्रा की बात करती है। आज के पाठकों को एक और परत दिखती है: चौबीस घंटे, पवित्र पत्थर में दर्ज।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shilpa-Surya with lunar phases drawn beside wheel
panels.action: By lamplight, Shilpa-Surya sketches crescents and full circles next to a wheel diagram, as outside the carved horses of the temple seem to strain forward in the moonlit night.

dialogue.text: Indian calendrical thought married solar days, lunar fortnights and months. Some scholars see hints of these rhythms in the Konark wheels’ number of divisions and the temple’s larger program.

i18n.hi: भारतीय पंचांग-चिंतन में सौर दिन, चंद्र पक्ष और महीने आपस में जुड़े थे। कुछ विद्वान कोणार्क के पहियों की बाँटों और पूरे मंदिर-योजना में इन लयों की झलक देखते हैं।

panels.shot: interior shot of Konark now, with visitor tracing shadow
panels.action: Centuries later, a modern visitor runs a fingertip along a wheel’s spoke as the late afternoon sun casts a shadow neatly between two carved markers.

dialogue.text: Konark is damaged; its main tower is gone. No inscription here spells out a sundial. Yet when a hand follows the shadow, the hour seems to hide within those carvings.

i18n.hi: कोणार्क घायल है; उसका मुख्य शिखर नहीं रहा। यहाँ कोई लेख इसे धूप-घड़ी नहीं कहता। फिर भी जब हाथ छाया के साथ चलता है, तो घंटे इन नक्काशियों में छुपे लगते हैं।

panels.shot: split frame: left, scholar’s chart; right, temple wheel in sun
panels.action: On one side, a scholar’s desk with printed charts from S. Balachandra Rao’s article; on the other, the real wheel at Konark catching harsh midday sun, the two images visually echoing each other.

dialogue.text: Rao’s argument is cautious but firm: the wheels are not mechanical clocks, but designed surfaces for reading solar time by shadow—a sophisticated fusion of art and applied astronomy.

i18n.hi: राव की दलील सावधान पर ठोस है: ये पहिये यांत्रिक घड़ियाँ नहीं, बल्कि धूप से समय पढ़ने के लिए बनाई गई सतहें हैं—कला और प्रयोगात्मक ज्योतिष का महीन संगम।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shilpa-Surya looking up at sun through scaffolding
panels.action: Shilpa-Surya stands amid bamboo scaffolding, eyes narrowed at the blazing sun, then turns toward the nearly finished wheels, his face lit with a quiet, satisfied resolve.

dialogue.text: We cannot hear the builders’ own words. But the field of Indian mathematics and astronomy—described by scholars like Kim Plofker—shows they lived in a culture used to thinking with angles and arcs.

i18n.hi: हम निर्माताओं की अपनी आवाज नहीं सुन पाते। पर भारतीय गणित और ज्योतिष का जगत—जिसे किम प्लोफकर जैसे विद्वान बताते हैं—दिखाता है कि वे कोणों और मेहराबों में सोचने के अभ्यस्त थे।

panels.shot: wide shot of temple base with wheels and seven horses
panels.action: A wide, majestic view shows the stone horses straining before the chariot base, the line of wheels glowing in slanting light, the sea haze softening the distant horizon.

dialogue.text: Kapila Vatsyayan wrote of the square and circle in Indian arts—the meeting of earth-plan and cosmic cycle. At Konark, the chariot base is the square; the wheels are the circles that keep its time.

i18n.hi: कपिला वात्स्यायन ने भारतीय कलाओं में चौकोर और गोल के मेल पर लिखा—भूमि-योजना और कॉस्मिक चक्र का संगम। कोणार्क में रथ का अधार चौकोर है; पहिये वे गोले हैं जो उसका समय थामते हैं।

panels.shot: close-up on Shilpa-Surya’s weathered hands on the stone rim
panels.action: His hands rest on the stone edge of a wheel, fingers tracing a carved division gently, as dust motes float in a beam of evening light.

dialogue.speaker: the_architects_of_konark
dialogue.text: Let the sun himself write the hours upon our work.

i18n.hi: घंटे सूरज ही हमारी रचना पर लिखे।

panels.shot: final wide at dusk, temple silhouette and wheel shadow fading
panels.action: As dusk falls, the Sun Temple stands in silhouette, its wheels dark against a violet sky; the last faint shadow on one rim melts into the stone as night rises from the sea.

dialogue.text: The architects of Konark left no memoir—only wheels that catch light. In them, beauty and measurement share the same circle, reminding us that science can speak softly through sacred art.

i18n.hi: कोणार्क के शिल्पी कोई आत्मकथा छोड़कर नहीं गए—बस ऐसे पहिये जो रोशनी पकड़ते हैं। इनमें सुंदरता और नाप एक ही गोले में मिलती है, याद दिलाती है कि विज्ञान पवित्र कला के भीतर धीमे स्वर में बोल सकता है।

title_i18n.en: The Wheels That Tell the Hour

subtitle_i18n.en: Stone Wheels, Silent Sun: Timekeeping at Konark
subtitle_i18n.hi: पत्थर के पहिये, मौन सूरज: कोणार्क की घड़ी
